messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticing p95/p99 write latency spikes on a subset of local NVMe drives in eu-west2 since ~02:10 UTC. GPU allocs are getting delayed ~20-40s when those hosts are selected.
infra-bot: [alert] nvme_iops_drop detected on cluster eu-west2-a. impacted_hosts: 12. severity: medium.
jamie: repro steps? metric graphs?
sam: quick snapshot: `iostat -x 1 3` shows avg await jumping 30ms -> 450ms on /dev/nvme0n1, write_qdepth growing. dmesg has repeated `blk_update_request: I/O error` on 3 hosts (not all).
ryan: any firmware rollouts recently?
maria: not that region — last nvme fw push was to us-west last week.
sam: I dug into placement logs: these hosts are on a single rack with older PMem-backed scratch pools; provisioning tends to pick them for small-batch GPU jobs because of affinity.
jamie: can we gate provisioning from these hosts until we triage? temporary routing rule?
ryan: yes, I can add a placement exclusion tag for rack-23 in eu-west2 for 10m. doing it now.
infra-bot: placement-rule-update: excluded tag `rack-23` for `gpu-provisioner` (ttl=10m).
maria: what's the failure mode — wear vs controller saturation vs filesystem?
sam: early signal looks like internal GC/latency wobble — SMART stays green but `/sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests` shows queue growth and `nvme error status` lines correlate with the p99 spikes. not yet seeing CRCs.
ryan: could be background trim/secure erase overlap with scrubber windows. any janitor jobs running?
jamie: scrub schedule shows a window at 02:00 in that AZ. we recently increased scrub parallelism globally.
maria: can we throttle scrub in that AZ only? prefer to reduce parallelism rather than disable.
ryan: will patch scrubber: set `max_parallel=2` for eu-west2 for the next maintenance window. applying now.
sam: logs (excerpt): ```
[02:12:04] nvme0n1: write qdepth 184 -> await 412ms
[02:12:05] nvme0n1: nvme status: code 0x1e timeout
[02:12:06] worker: retrying write (attempt 2) host=gnode-523
```
jamie: we should also move existing pending GPU jobs off those hosts to avoid tails. can we drain?
ryan: initiating soft drain on the 12 hosts — marking as unschedulable for new GPU attaches, migrating lightweight pods now.
sam: note: this will increase provisioning latency cluster-wide by ~5% while drain completes.
maria: cost check — if we keep many hosts excluded and fall back to preemptible pools, runtime costs could spike. we need to balance.
jamie: short term safety>cost. long term we need telemetry to detect GC wobble earlier.
ryan: opened ticket INF-9843: add per-host NVMe GC telemetry + early throttling hook. linking: https://redwood.internal/INF-9843
sam: action list: 1) exclude rack-23 for 10m (done). 2) soft-drain 12 hosts (in progress). 3) reduce scrubber parallelism in eu-west2 (patch applied). 4) collect nvme controller logs and SMART dump from affected hosts — I'll run that.
maria: pls add a quick runbook note for oncall: `if nvme await>200ms and CRC==0 and smart_ok==true -> throttle scrub parallelism + soft drain`.
jamie: agreed. adding note to runbook now.
infra-bot: incident-note: INF-2026 created for eu-west2 nvme latency wobble. severity=low->monitor.
sam: pulling SMART/dmesg and putting artifacts in ticket. won't escalate unless CRCs show or host count increases.
ryan: I'll revert placement exclusion after 10m and monitor. if it recurs we'll do a deeper kernel/module rollback test.
maria: thanks everyone. post-mortem if INF-2026 remains open after 24h. :raised_hands:
sam: update @1735020450 — SMARTs look nominal, controller logs show frequent `GC phase start` spikes. copying logs to INF-9843. un-excluding rack-23 now to re-evaluate under light load.
jamie: nice work. let's follow up with long-term mitigations in INF-9843.
